observation_summary: The application throws a NullPointerException instead of an AssertionError when a null value is passed to the 'same' matcher, causing an unexpected exception during verification.
hypothesis: The 'Same' matcher's 'describeTo' method attempts to call 'toString()' on a 'wanted' object without checking if it is null, leading to a NullPointerException when 'same(null)' is used.
prediction: The code will contain a call to 'wanted.toString()' without a null check. Adding a ternary operator or an if-statement to handle the null case will resolve the issue.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the code was changed from 'description.appendText(wanted.toString())' to 'description.appendText(wanted == null ? "null" : wanted.toString())'. This confirms that the root cause was a missing null check on the 'wanted' object.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic missing null check (guard) in the 'describeTo' method. The code assumes 'wanted' is non-null, but the 'same' matcher supports null arguments. Adding the null check prevents the NullPointerException, which is the definition of a 'Checking' ODC type.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows a NullPointerException.
The fix diff shows the addition of a null check: 'wanted == null ? "null" : wanted.toString()'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not about an incorrect value being assigned, but about the lack of a guard condition before performing an operation on a potentially null object.
The logic is not fundamentally flawed in its procedure; it simply lacks a necessary validation check for the input parameter.
